Sticky foods.Honey: Honey is a supersaturated sugar solution, so thick and tacky that bees fan it to evaporate water. A jar can last for centuries.
Sticky foods.Caramel: Caramel sticks to your teeth because melted sugar cools into an amorphous, tacky glass-like state, softened by butter and milk.
Sticky foods.Maple syrup: Syrup that clings to the plate is boiled sap, and it takes about 40 liters of it to make one liter of syrup.
Sticky foods.Toffee: Toffee can go from sticky to brittle depending on the temperature it reaches. Sticky toffee pudding is a British classic.
Sticky foods.Molasses: A thick, dark syrup left over when sugar is refined. Its stickiness once fueled a 1919 Boston disaster when a tank burst.
Sticky foods.Marshmallow: Gelatin and sugar make it tacky, which is why it clings to graham crackers and fingers when you roast one.
Sticky foods.Peanut butter: It sticks to the roof of your mouth because it's a thick paste of fat and protein. Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts.
Sticky foods.Sticky rice: Glutinous rice, high in amylopectin starch, clumps tightly. It contains no gluten, despite the name.
Sticky foods.Cotton candy: Spun sugar threads are sticky because they quickly absorb water from the air and dissolve slightly on your fingers.
Sticky foods.Taffy: Taffy is pulled repeatedly, which adds air and gives it a chewy stretch. The Jersey Shore made saltwater taffy famous.
Sticky foods.Nutella: A hazelnut and cocoa spread invented in Italy in the 1960s. Its stickiness comes from fat, sugar and ground nuts.
Sticky foods.Mochi: Pounded glutinous rice that stays stretchy and clings to everything. It's a New Year tradition in Japan, and a known choking hazard.
Sticky foods.Crackers: Crackers are dry, thin and crisp, so they don't stick to much at all, which is the point.
Sticky foods.Popcorn: Popcorn is dry and fluffy. It only gets sticky when coated in caramel or syrup, like in caramel corn.
Sticky foods.Celery: Celery is fibrous and watery, not sticky. Its strings are bundles of tough fibers that run along the stalk.
Sticky foods.Rice cake: Puffed rice cakes are dry and crisp. The sticky kind, like Korean tteok, is a different thing entirely.
Sticky foods.Water: Water isn't tacky, though its surface tension makes drops cling to each other and to a surface.
Sticky foods.Ice cube: Ice can briefly stick to a wet finger, but that's freezing moisture, not stickiness.
Sticky foods.Almonds: Almonds are dry and crunchy. Almond butter is thick but oily, and not truly tacky.
Sticky foods.Lettuce: Lettuce is crisp and mostly water, about 95 percent, with nothing sticky about it.
Sticky foods.Salt: Salt is dry, though it can clump in humid weather as it absorbs moisture from the air.
Sticky foods.Croutons: Croutons are dry, hard bread cubes with no tackiness.
Sticky foods.Potato chips: Chips are thin, crisp and oily, but not sticky, and most of the water is fried out.
Sticky foods.Pretzels: Hard pretzels are dry and crunchy. Soft ones are chewy and a bit tacky, but they aren't sticky like caramel.

Sounds a dog makes.Bark: The classic dog sound. Dogs bark far more than wolves do, a trait likely amplified during domestication.
Sounds a dog makes.Woof: The English spelling of a dog's bark. Other languages hear it differently: wan-wan in Japanese, wau-wau in German.
Sounds a dog makes.Growl: A low warning sound, often used when a dog feels threatened or protective of food. It is communication, not always aggression.
Sounds a dog makes.Howl: A long, rising cry that dogs share with wolves, and it can carry for kilometres. Some dogs howl at sirens.
Sounds a dog makes.Whine: A high-pitched sound dogs use to ask for attention, show anxiety, or beg, and puppies use it to call their mother.
Sounds a dog makes.Yelp: A sharp, short cry of pain or surprise. Puppies use it to tell littermates when play bites get too rough.
Sounds a dog makes.Snarl: A growl with bared teeth, a clear last warning. Dogs usually show this before biting.
Sounds a dog makes.Whimper: A soft, quiet cry, often showing fear or pain. Puppies whimper when they're cold or separated from their mother.
Sounds a dog makes.Bay: The deep, drawn-out cry of hounds on a scent. It's why hunting dogs are said to be at bay, and the sound carries over long distances.
Sounds a dog makes.Arf: A comic-strip spelling of a dog bark. It was famously used by the cartoon dog Little Orphan Annie's Sandy.
Sounds a dog makes.Yip: A short, high-pitched bark of small dogs and puppies. Coyotes also yip, as do foxes.
Sounds a dog makes.Meow: A cat sound, and almost purely a trap here. Adult cats mostly meow at humans, not at each other.
Sounds a dog makes.Purr: A cat sound produced in the throat at about 25 to 150 vibrations per second, and it may promote healing.
Sounds a dog makes.Moo: The cow's call. Cows can have regional accents, in a sense, as herds develop slightly different calls.
Sounds a dog makes.Neigh: The horse's call. Horses can make two different sounds at once, using their larynx in a special way.
Sounds a dog makes.Oink: A pig's grunt. Mother pigs sing to their piglets while nursing, and piglets learn to answer their own mother's voice.
Sounds a dog makes.Quack: The duck's call. The idea that a duck's quack does not echo is an urban myth.
Sounds a dog makes.Baa: A sheep's sound. A lamb and its mother can recognise each other's voices among hundreds of others.
Sounds a dog makes.Chirp: A short, high note of small birds and crickets. Not a dog sound, even though dogs may chirp to puppies in rare cases.
Sounds a dog makes.Bleat: The sound of sheep and goats. It is not a dog sound, but can sound like a high whine.
Sounds a dog makes.Croak: The call of frogs, toads, and ravens. Many frogs use vocal sacs to amplify the sound.
Sounds a dog makes.Hoot: An owl's call. Different owls hoot in very different ways, which helps birders tell them apart at night.
Sounds a dog makes.Cluck: A chicken sound. Hens use different clucks to call chicks to food or to warn of danger.
Sounds a dog makes.Bray: A donkey's loud call, which can be heard for about 3 kilometres. It is a known sound of donkeys, not dogs.

French wine regions.Bordeaux: Home of Cabernet and Merlot blends, the area ships hundreds of millions of bottles, and its 1855 classification of châteaux still rules the top estates.
French wine regions.Burgundy: Home of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, its vineyards are split into tiny named plots called climats, which hold UNESCO World Heritage status.
French wine regions.Champagne: Only sparkling wine from this region can legally carry its name. The Benedictine monk Dom Pérignon is commonly credited with perfecting it, though he did not invent fizz.
French wine regions.Loire: The Loire is France's longest river and its valley makes everything from Muscadet to Sancerre. Hundreds of châteaux line the banks.
French wine regions.Alsace: A French region on the German border, whose Rhine-side wines are usually bottled in tall, slim flutes and named after the grape, which is rare in France.
French wine regions.Rhône: A river valley region of the south-east that makes Châteauneuf-du-Pape. The name of the Papal winery reflects the popes' stay in nearby Avignon.
French wine regions.Provence: The world's pink-wine capital: about 90 percent of the wine made here is rosé, and it has been making it since Greek colonists arrived over 2,000 years ago.
French wine regions.Beaujolais: A region that grows Gamay, whose wines are released as Nouveau every third Thursday of November, a few weeks after harvest.
French wine regions.Languedoc: The world's largest wine-producing region by volume, in the south of France. It once made so much cheap wine that France called it a 'wine lake'.
French wine regions.Chablis: The northernmost Burgundy district, with limestone soils full of fossil oyster shells; its steely unoaked Chardonnay is prized with seafood.
French wine regions.Sauternes: A Bordeaux area where noble rot concentrates the grapes into golden, syrupy dessert wine. Château d'Yquem is the most famous estate.
French wine regions.Médoc: A Bordeaux area on the left bank of the Gironde, famous for gravelly Cabernet Sauvignon and the Margaux and Pauillac names.
French wine regions.Rioja: A trap: this is Spain's most famous red wine region, in the north. Its wines are aged in oak, and not French.
French wine regions.Chianti: A Tuscan region in Italy and its wine, whose black rooster emblem is on bottles. Not French.
French wine regions.Tuscany: A trap: the region around Florence in Italy, famous for Chianti and Brunello. It is Italian, not French.
French wine regions.Napa: California's most famous valley, where the 1976 Judgment of Paris tasting beat France. It's American, not French.
French wine regions.Barolo: A trap: Piedmont's 'king of wines', made from Nebbiolo grapes in northwest Italy. It is Italian, not French.
French wine regions.Mosel: Germany's river valley, where Riesling grows on very steep slate slopes above the water. German, not French.
French wine regions.Douro: Portugal's river valley, whose terraced vineyards make port. The oldest legally demarcated wine region in the world, from 1756.
French wine regions.Marlborough: New Zealand's South Island region, famous for zesty Sauvignon Blanc that put the country on the wine map.
French wine regions.Barossa: Australia's South Australian valley, known for old-vine Shiraz, some vines are over 150 years old, and it's German-settled.
French wine regions.Mendoza: Argentina's high-altitude region at the foot of the Andes, the home of Malbec. Not French.
French wine regions.Sonoma: A trap: this California county neighbours Napa and is known for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It is American, not French.
French wine regions.Tokaj: A Hungarian region famous for sweet Tokaji, once called the 'wine of kings and king of wines'. It's Hungarian.

Indonesian islands.Java: Over half of Indonesia's people live on this one island, which includes the capital Jakarta, and its coffee gave "java" its meaning.
Indonesian islands.Sumatra: One of the last places where tigers, rhinos, orangutans and elephants all share the same wild landscape.
Indonesian islands.Bali: A Hindu island in a mostly Muslim nation, where Nyepi, the Day of Silence, shuts down everything, even the airport.
Indonesian islands.Sulawesi: A strangely shaped island with four peninsulas, often compared to a spiky orchid or a letter K.
Indonesian islands.Lombok: Just east of Bali across a deep strait, it is dominated by the volcano Mount Rinjani, a popular trek.
Indonesian islands.Komodo: Home to the Komodo dragon, the world's heaviest lizard, which can reach about 3 metres in length.
Indonesian islands.Flores: In 2003, bones of a tiny extinct human species, nicknamed the hobbit, were found on this island.
Indonesian islands.Sumba: Famous for woven ikat textiles and for the Pasola, a festival where horsemen throw blunt spears at each other.
Indonesian islands.Ambon: Part of the Maluku or Spice Islands, whose cloves and nutmeg once drew European fleets across the world.
Indonesian islands.Madura: Famed for karapan sapi, bull races in which pairs of bulls pull a jockey on a wooden sled at high speed.
Indonesian islands.Luzon: The largest island of the Philippines, home to Manila, so it is Philippine, not Indonesian.
Indonesian islands.Mindanao: The second-largest island in the Philippines, with its own mountains and volcanoes, but not Indonesian.
Indonesian islands.Cebu: A central Philippine island where Magellan was killed in 1521, and a hub for diving.
Indonesian islands.Palawan: A Philippine island close to Borneo, famed for its underground river, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Indonesian islands.Boracay: A small Philippine island with a famous white-sand beach, belonging to the Philippines.
Indonesian islands.Phuket: Thailand's largest island, in the Andaman Sea, with beaches that draw millions, not Indonesian.
Indonesian islands.Ko Samui: A Thai island in the Gulf of Thailand, known for coconut plantations and beaches.
Indonesian islands.Penang: A Malaysian island whose capital George Town is a UNESCO site and a celebrated street food capital.
Indonesian islands.Langkawi: An archipelago off north-west Malaysia, with a duty-free status and a cable car, not Indonesian.
Indonesian islands.Sri Lanka: It is an independent island country in the Indian Ocean, not part of Indonesia, and was once known as Ceylon.
Indonesian islands.Okinawa: A subtropical Japanese island chain, famed for its long-lived residents and as the birthplace of karate.
Indonesian islands.Hainan: China's island province in the South China Sea, sometimes called the Hawaii of China.
Indonesian islands.Jeju: A volcanic South Korean island, where female free-divers called haenyeo gather seafood without oxygen tanks.
Indonesian islands.Tasmania: An Australian island state south of the mainland, home to the Tasmanian devil.

Robots from film and TV.R2-D2: His beeps were created by sound designer Ben Burtt using synthesizers and his own voice, and Kenny Baker operated the original on set.
Robots from film and TV.C-3PO: Anthony Daniels wore a hot, rigid gold suit, and in the first film he couldn't sit or even easily bend his arms.
Robots from film and TV.WALL-E: Pixar's trash-compacting robot says almost nothing, relying on sound design by Ben Burtt, who also created R2-D2's voice.
Robots from film and TV.EVE: The sleek white probe in WALL-E was designed with inspiration from Apple's products, as director Andrew Stanton asked for the 'iPod of robots'.
Robots from film and TV.Baymax: The soft, inflatable healthcare robot of Big Hero 6 was inspired by real soft robotics research at Carnegie Mellon University.
Robots from film and TV.Optimus Prime: Peter Cullen's deep voice for the Autobot leader has been used since the 1980s, and he turns into a big-rig truck.
Robots from film and TV.Johnny 5: The Short Circuit robot comes alive after a lightning strike, and he famously shouts 'Need input!' while reading books at lightning speed.
Robots from film and TV.Bumblebee: In the original cartoon the little yellow Autobot turned into a Volkswagen Beetle; the live-action films later made him a Camaro.
Robots from film and TV.The Iron Giant: Brad Bird's 1999 film ends with the giant choosing to sacrifice himself, and the scene has made many viewers cry.
Robots from film and TV.Robby the Robot: Robby debuted in 1956's Forbidden Planet and later popped up on shows like The Twilight Zone, becoming one of the first famous movie robots.
Robots from film and TV.Megatron: The Decepticon leader transforms into a handgun in the original toy line, a detail changed in later versions.
Robots from film and TV.BB-8: The rolling droid of The Force Awakens was built as a real working prop, partly using magnets to keep his head on his body.
Robots from film and TV.Rosie: The Jetsons' robot maid is a fan favorite and a reminder that 1960s cartoons imagined household robots decades before Roombas.
Robots from film and TV.Bender: The Futurama robot's full name is Bender Bending Rodriguez, and he runs on alcohol, which he loves to drink.
Spielberg's 1982 alien isn't a robot but a biological creature, and Reese's Pieces got a sales boost from his film.
Robots from film and TV.Groot: Groot is a tree-like alien, a living plant rather than a machine, and his only words are 'I am Groot'.
Robots from film and TV.Stitch: Stitch is a genetically engineered alien experiment from Lilo & Stitch, not a robot.
Robots from film and TV.Chewbacca: Chewbacca is a Wookiee, an organic alien species, and his roar was created from animal sounds like bears.
Robots from film and TV.Yoda: Yoda is a green, 900-year-old Jedi Master, an alien rather than a machine, and was originally a puppet operated by Frank Oz.
Robots from film and TV.Godzilla: Godzilla is a giant radioactive monster, first appearing in a 1954 Japanese film, not a robot, though 'Mechagodzilla' is one.
Robots from film and TV.King Kong: Kong is a giant ape from 1933, a living creature and not a robot.
Robots from film and TV.Gizmo: Gizmo is a furry mogwai from Gremlins, and he's an organic creature, not a machine.
Robots from film and TV.Totoro: Totoro is a forest spirit from Studio Ghibli's My Neighbor Totoro, and he's not a robot.
Robots from film and TV.ALF: ALF, from the planet Melmac, is a furry alien who loves to eat cats in the 1980s sitcom, so he isn't a robot.

Cartoon ducks.Donald Duck: Donald debuted in 1934's The Wise Little Hen, and Clarence Nash's famous quacking voice was his trademark.
Cartoon ducks.Daffy Duck: Daffy first appeared in 1937's Porky's Duck Hunt, with a lisping screwball voice from Mel Blanc.
Cartoon ducks.Scrooge McDuck: Carl Barks introduced Scrooge in 1947, and named him after Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge.
Cartoon ducks.Darkwing Duck: Darkwing, the 'terror that flaps in the night', parodies Batman and spun off from Disney's DuckTales.
Cartoon ducks.Daisy Duck: Daisy debuted in 1940 as Donald's girlfriend, in the cartoon Mr. Duck Steps Out.
Cartoon ducks.Huey: Huey, Dewey and Louie first appeared in a 1937 comic strip, as the nephews of Donald Duck.
Cartoon ducks.Dewey: In the 2017 DuckTales reboot, Dewey is the adventurous, reckless triplet, and wears blue.
Cartoon ducks.Louie: In the 2017 DuckTales, Louie became the schemer of the trio, in green, to give each triplet a distinct personality.
Cartoon ducks.Howard the Duck: Marvel's cigar-chomping Howard debuted in 1973, and the 1986 George Lucas-produced film flopped.
Cartoon ducks.Plucky Duck: Plucky is Daffy-like, and appears with Buster Bunny in Tiny Toon Adventures.
Cartoon ducks.Launchpad McQuack: Launchpad is the DuckTales pilot who crashes constantly, and he idolizes Darkwing Duck.
Cartoon ducks.Psyduck: Psyduck, number 54 in the Pokedex, is a Pokemon with a permanent headache, which unlocks its psychic powers.
Cartoon ducks.Count Duckula: Count Duckula is a vegetarian vampire duck from a British 1988 cartoon, who hates blood.
Cartoon ducks.Woody Woodpecker: Woody is a woodpecker, not a duck, and his manic laugh was first performed by Mel Blanc.
Cartoon ducks.Tweety: Tweety is a canary, not a duck, who first appeared nearly bald and pink in 1942.
Cartoon ducks.Foghorn Leghorn: Foghorn is a rooster, inspired by a radio character, Senator Claghorn.
Cartoon ducks.Road Runner: The Road Runner says 'beep beep', and real roadrunners can run about 20 miles per hour.
Cartoon ducks.Woodstock: Woodstock is Snoopy's tiny yellow bird, named for the 1969 music festival.
Cartoon ducks.Zazu: Zazu is a red-billed hornbill in The Lion King, not a duck.
Cartoon ducks.Iago: Iago is a parrot, and Gilbert Gottfried, who voiced him, also voiced the Aflac Duck.
Cartoon ducks.Heihei: Heihei is a rooster, and domestic chickens descended from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia.
Cartoon ducks.Scuttle: Scuttle is a seagull in The Little Mermaid, and he misidentifies human objects with great confidence.
Cartoon ducks.Big Bird: Big Bird, 8 feet 2 inches tall, was puppeteered for decades by Caroll Spinney, and is a canary-like bird, not a duck.
Cartoon ducks.Chicken Little: Chicken Little panics that the sky is falling in a folk tale as old as the 1800s.

Bands from Australia.AC/DC: AC/DC formed in Sydney in 1973 by Scottish-born brothers Malcolm and Angus Young, and Back in Black ranks among the best-selling albums ever.
Bands from Australia.INXS: INXS came from Sydney, fronted by Michael Hutchence, and their hits include Need You Tonight and Never Tear Us Apart.
Bands from Australia.Men at Work: Down Under made Men at Work a US number one, and a court later found its flute riff borrowed from Kookaburra.
Bands from Australia.Midnight Oil: Midnight Oil's singer Peter Garrett later became an Australian government minister, an unusual path for a rock star.
Bands from Australia.Tame Impala: Tame Impala is mostly Perth's Kevin Parker, who plays and produces nearly all the instruments himself.
Bands from Australia.5 Seconds of Summer: 5 Seconds of Summer started in Sydney by posting covers online, and then toured as support for One Direction.
Bands from Australia.Savage Garden: Savage Garden, with singer Darren Hayes, had a global hit with Truly Madly Deeply, from Queensland.
Bands from Australia.Wolfmother: Wolfmother's Woman, from Sydney, earned a Grammy, and the band's sound was often compared with Led Zeppelin.
Bands from Australia.The Wiggles: The Wiggles began in 1991, formed by early-childhood education students, and became hugely successful with kids' music.
Bands from Australia.Silverchair: Silverchair formed as teenagers in Newcastle, NSW, and their debut Frogstomp topped Australian charts in 1995.
Bands from Australia.Air Supply: Air Supply formed in Sydney in 1975 after the two founders met in a cast of Jesus Christ Superstar.
Bands from Australia.U2: U2 is from Dublin, Ireland, so they're an easy Irish trap here.
Bands from Australia.Oasis: Oasis are from Manchester, England, and they dominated British charts in the 1990s.
Bands from Australia.The Killers: The Killers formed in Las Vegas, and Mr. Brightside, from 2004, is still hugely popular.
Bands from Australia.Nickelback: Nickelback comes from Hanna, Alberta, in Canada, and not from Australia.
Bands from Australia.Rush: Rush was a Toronto trio, so they're Canadian, with Neil Peart as their celebrated drummer.
Bands from Australia.Arcade Fire: Arcade Fire formed in Montreal, Canada, and won the Album of the Year Grammy in 2011 for The Suburbs.
Bands from Australia.ABBA: ABBA is Swedish, and a huge worldwide success after winning Eurovision in 1974.
Bands from Australia.Coldplay: Coldplay is British, formed in London while the members were at university.
Bands from Australia.Metallica: Metallica was formed in Los Angeles in 1981, with Danish-born drummer Lars Ulrich.
Bands from Australia.Foo Fighters: Foo Fighters formed in Seattle in 1994, after Dave Grohl, Nirvana's drummer, recorded their first album on his own.
Bands from Australia.Kings of Leon: Kings of Leon are from Tennessee, brothers and a cousin, and they're an American Southern band.
Bands from Australia.Def Leppard: Def Leppard formed in Sheffield, England, and their drummer Rick Allen kept playing after losing an arm.
Bands from Australia.Daft Punk: Daft Punk was French, from Paris, so only an Australian-sounding trap for Tame Impala fans.

Songs with weather in the title.Ain't No Sunshine: Bill Withers repeats 'I know' 26 times in the song, which he wrote after watching the film Days of Wine and Roses.

Songs with weather in the title.Candle in the Wind: Written about Marilyn Monroe and rewritten for Diana, it counts here because of the wind in the title.

Songs with weather in the title.Hey Jude: Beatles' 1968 hit for Julian Lennon. No weather here, despite the sad feeling.
Songs with weather in the title.Firework: Katy Perry's 2010 anthem. Fireworks light up the sky, but fireworks are not weather.
Songs with weather in the title.Rocket Man: Elton John's 1972 song about an astronaut, no weather in the lyrics.

Songs with weather in the title.Moon River: Written by Henry Mancini for Breakfast at Tiffany's, Audrey Hepburn sings it on the fire escape. A river, not weather.
Songs with weather in the title.Hotel California: Eagles' 1976 classic, set in a mythical hotel. Warm desert wind is only mentioned, not the theme.
